candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide age-appropriate injury-prevention and health-promotion teaching for infants and families, including environmental exposure prevention and anticipatory guidance.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — infant ultraviolet/sun protection
candidate.educational_objective: Protect infants younger than 6 months from ultraviolet exposure primarily with shade, avoidance of direct sunlight and protective clothing, and consult a clinician before using sunscreen.

options.A: Use sunscreen as the primary protection for the infant because shade and clothing provide insufficient ultraviolet protection.
options.B: Provide brief direct midday sun exposure each day because infants younger than 6 months are less susceptible to sunburn.
options.C: Apply an adult sunscreen routinely to all exposed skin before using shade or protective clothing.
options.D: Keep the infant out of direct sunlight when possible, use shade and protective clothing, and ask the pediatrician or another clinician before applying sunscreen.

candidate.rationale: Current FDA guidance states that sunscreen is not generally recommended for infants younger than 6 months because their skin is more vulnerable to sunscreen adverse effects. The best protection is to keep infants out of direct sunlight, use shade and protective clothing when outdoors, and consult a doctor before applying sunscreen to a child younger than 6 months. Therefore D is correct. A and C make sunscreen the primary or routine first-line protection contrary to FDA guidance, while B exposes the infant during peak-intensity sunlight and falsely assumes reduced sunburn susceptibility.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For infants younger than 6 months, FDA recommends avoiding direct sun, using shade and protective clothing, and consulting a clinician before applying sunscreen rather than relying on sunscreen as the primary protective measure.
candidate.source_document_title: Should You Put Sunscreen on Infants? Not Usually; Sunscreen: How to Help Protect Your Skin from the Sun
